providers.name: Haven Women's Health & Birth Center
providers.services: Prenatal care, labor and birth (including water birth), postpartum care through six weeks, well-woman care, breastfeeding support, birth center tours
providers.serviceArea: Cary, NC and surrounding Triangle area
providers.costRange: Not published; pricing and insurance questions are addressed during a free birth center tour/orientation
providers.description: Haven Women's Health & Birth Center is a midwifery-led birth center in Cary, NC founded in 2024 by Sara Fawson, who has worked in women's health and birth care in the Triangle since 2018. The center reports 200+ babies delivered since 2004 and a 5% cesarean rate for mothers who begin labor at the birth center (https://www.havenhealthandbirth.com/). It is located at 226 Ashville Ave, Suite 20, Cary, NC 27518, in close proximity to WakeMed Cary Hospital for transfers (https://www.havenhealthandbirth.com/).

providers.name: Triangle Doula by Nature
providers.credential: Birth doula (Ka'Tiera Truett, trained birth professional)
providers.services: Birth doula support, childbirth education, birth plan consultations, prenatal and postpartum visits, support for hospital, home, water, and birth center births
providers.serviceArea: Raleigh, Durham, Cary, Chapel Hill, Carrboro, Hillsborough, Apex, Wake Forest, Garner and other NC Triangle and Triad cities
providers.description: Triangle Doula by Nature is a birth doula practice serving families in Cary and across the NC Triangle and Triad, offering prenatal, labor, and postpartum support (https://www.triangledoulabynature.com/). The practice supports a wide range of birth goals including hospital, home, water, and birth center births, as well as VBAC and cesarean births (https://www.triangledoulabynature.com/).

providers.name: Amanda Petry
providers.services: Lactation and breastfeeding support, in-home visits, pumping and milk supply guidance, support for premature infants and multiples
providers.description: Amanda Petry is a Registered Nurse and International Board Certified Lactation Consultant based in Cary, NC who provides personalized infant feeding support from pregnancy through the breastfeeding journey (https://www.bornbir.com/amanda-petry). She offers in-home visits for reassurance and troubleshooting, and has experience supporting premature infants, multiples, and a range of feeding challenges (https://www.bornbir.com/amanda-petry).

providers.name: Sacred Haven Midwifery
providers.services: CNM-led home birth, prenatal and postpartum care
providers.description: Sacred Haven Midwifery is a Certified Nurse-Midwife led homebirth team serving women and families in North Carolina (https://www.sacredhavenmidwifery.com/). The practice is based in Selma, NC and provides home birth care across the state (https://www.centralcarolinadoulas.com/homebirth-options-fayettevillenc/).

providers.name: Mariam Lam
providers.services: Birth doula support, prenatal and postpartum visits, on-call labor support
providers.serviceArea: Durham, NC and surrounding Triangle area including Cary
providers.description: Mariam Lam is a DONA International certified birth doula serving the Durham and Triangle area, listed among birth doulas available to Cary families on the Meela directory (https://www.hellomeela.com/cary-nc/doulas/). She has supported 50 families over 6 years and lists a $900 birth fee on her profile (https://www.hellomeela.com/cary-nc/doulas/).

hospitals.name: WakeMed Cary Hospital
hospitals.doula_policy: Not published on WakeMed's public pages; doula access is typically coordinated with the care team
hospitals.description: WakeMed Cary Hospital is the inpatient hospital serving western Wake County and offers a full maternity program with labor and delivery, postpartum care, and lactation support (https://www.wakemed.org/find-a-location/cary-hospital/services-and-specialties/pregnancy-and-childbirth). The hospital has a Level III NICU that provides care for babies needing short-term intensive care, sharing a full-time staff of neonatologists and 24-hour neonatal nurse practitioners with the Raleigh Campus (https://www.wakemed.org/find-a-location/cary-hospital/services-and-specialties/pregnancy-and-childbirth/nicu). Babies who need a higher level of care can be transferred to the Raleigh Campus via the Children's Transport Team, and the mother is moved to the Women's Pavilion & Birthplace in Raleigh when possible (https://www.wakemed.org/find-a-location/cary-hospital/services-and-specialties/pregnancy-and-childbirth/nicu). The hospital offers free guided tours of the birthing center on weekday evenings and one Saturday per month, plus a virtual tour (https://www.wakemed.org/find-a-location/cary-hospital/services-and-specialties/pregnancy-and-childbirth/take-a-tour). Care teams include labor and delivery nurses, obstetrical hospitalists, anesthesiologists, and lactation consultants (https://www.wakemed.org/find-a-location/cary-hospital/services-and-specialties/pregnancy-and-childbirth).

hospitals.name: UNC Health Rex (Rex Women's Center)
hospitals.doula_policy: A doula is considered one of the three visitors allowed at the bedside
hospitals.description: UNC Health Rex's Rex Women's Center in Raleigh is a major maternity destination in the Triangle, reporting that it delivers more babies than any other hospital in the region (https://www.rexhealth.com/rh/care-treatment/womens-health/maternity-services/labor-delivery/). The center provides a birth center with private labor and delivery rooms, and its care team includes obstetricians, OB hospitalists, certified nurse midwives, neonatologists, and lactation consultants (https://www.rexhealth.com/rh/care-treatment/womens-health/maternity-services/). Its Neonatal Intensive Care Unit holds a Level IV designation, allowing care for the most premature and medically fragile babies (https://www.rexhealth.com/rh/about/news-media/2015/november/rex-womens-center-neonatal-intensive-care-unit-receives-level-iv/). The Rex Women's Center visitation policy allows three visitors at the bedside, and a doula is considered one of the three visitors (https://www.rexhealth.com/rh/care-treatment/womens-health/maternity-services/labor-delivery/). The center also offers maternal-fetal medicine specialists for high-risk pregnancies and an OB emergency department staffed by OB hospitalists (https://www.rexhealth.com/rh/care-treatment/womens-health/maternity-services/).

birth_centers.name: Haven Women's Health & Birth Center
birth_centers.description: A CNM-led, CABC-accredited birth center in Cary offering prenatal care, water birth, labor and birth suites, and postpartum care through six weeks. It is located in close proximity to WakeMed Cary Hospital for transfers. Free weekly birth center tours are offered for pricing and insurance questions.

midwife_info.summary: North Carolina licenses Certified Nurse-Midwives (CNMs) through the NC Board of Nursing; Certified Professional Midwives (CPMs) are not currently licensed in the state, so only CNMs may legally attend births, including planned home births where they choose to offer them (https://www.homebirthpartners.com/directory/north-carolina/). A 2023 state law (S.L. 2023-14) ended the decades-old physician supervision requirement for CNMs with at least 24 months and 4,000 hours of practice, while newer CNMs work under a collaborative provider agreement (https://www.homebirthpartners.com/directory/north-carolina/).

birth_stats.cesarean_rate: 31% of all live births in North Carolina in 2023 (KFF, based on CDC NCHS National Vital Statistics System)
birth_stats.maternal_mortality: 26.7 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births in North Carolina, 2018-2022 (159 deaths; KFF, based on CDC NCHS)
birth_stats.home_birth_rate: 0.96% of live births in North Carolina took place at home in 2023 (1,155 home births), up from 0.5% (604) in 2019
birth_stats.infant_mortality: 6.24 infant deaths per 1,000 live births in North Carolina (2024, CDC NCHS)

culture: Cary is a fast-growing town in the Research Triangle region of North Carolina, located between Raleigh and Research Triangle Park, and is known for its family-oriented neighborhoods, highly rated schools, and extensive parks and greenways (https://www.tcrnc.com/cary-guide). The town has a highly educated population, with 70.5% of residents age 25 and older holding a bachelor's degree or higher and a median household income of $134,905 (2020-2024 ACS, U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts) (https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/carytownnorthcarolina/PST045225). Expectant families in Cary benefit from proximity to multiple maternity options, including the local WakeMed Cary Hospital, the larger UNC Health Rex in nearby Raleigh, and a freestanding birth center within the town itself. The broader Triangle is home to a strong midwifery and doula community, with the UNC School of Nursing and UNC Midwifery program contributing to a deep CNM talent pool (https://www.homebirthpartners.com/directory/north-carolina/).
hero_local_detail: Cary families can choose between the local WakeMed Cary Hospital, which offers a Level III NICU and a full maternity program at 1900 Kildaire Farm Road, and the larger UNC Health Rex in Raleigh, about 20 minutes away, which has a Level IV NICU and allows a doula as one of three bedside visitors (https://www.wakemed.org/find-a-location/cary-hospital/services-and-specialties/pregnancy-and-childbirth; https://www.rexhealth.com/rh/care-treatment/womens-health/maternity-services/labor-delivery/). For out-of-hospital birth, Haven Women's Health & Birth Center operates a CNM-led birth center in Cary with water birth suites and a 5% cesarean rate for clients who begin labor there, located close to WakeMed Cary for transfers (https://www.havenhealthandbirth.com/).

faqs.question: What hospitals offer labor and delivery near Cary, NC?
faqs.answer: WakeMed Cary Hospital (1900 Kildaire Farm Road, Cary) provides labor and delivery, postpartum care, and a Level III NICU. UNC Health Rex in Raleigh (4420 Lake Boone Trail) offers a Level IV NICU and a birth center with private labor and delivery rooms. Both are within roughly 20-30 minutes of most of Cary.

faqs.question: Is there a birth center in Cary, NC?
faqs.answer: Yes. Haven Women's Health & Birth Center is a CNM-led, CABC-accredited birth center at 226 Ashville Ave, Suite 20, Cary, NC 27518, offering prenatal care, water birth, and postpartum care, with free weekly tours for pricing and insurance questions.

faqs.question: Can a doula attend a birth at WakeMed Cary Hospital or UNC Health Rex?
faqs.answer: UNC Health Rex's Rex Women's Center explicitly counts a doula as one of the three visitors allowed at the bedside. WakeMed Cary Hospital does not publish a specific doula policy on its public pages, so doula access should be confirmed with the care team.

faqs.question: Are Certified Professional Midwives (CPMs) licensed in North Carolina?
faqs.answer: No. North Carolina licenses Certified Nurse-Midwives (CNMs) through the NC Board of Nursing, but CPMs are not currently licensed in the state. Only CNMs may legally attend births in North Carolina, including planned home births where they choose to offer them.

faqs.question: What is the cesarean rate in North Carolina?
faqs.answer: In 2023, 31% of all live births in North Carolina were cesarean deliveries, with a low-risk cesarean rate of 25%, according to KFF data based on the CDC NCHS National Vital Statistics System.
